text: I'll start by laying out the honeycomb cell grid in 2D and checking the hexagon orientation and clipping against the duct section.
Orientation confirmed: 8 mm across flats in y, 9.2376 across corners in x. Now the staggered grid clipped to the duct section inset by one wall thickness.
93 cells, smallest fragment 50 % of a full cell, open area 72.9 %. Let me look at the section before extruding.
The fill polygons are drawn from unordered vertices; let me redraw from edge geometry to see the real outlines.
Now the 3D solid: cells extruded through the full 20 mm, plate = core box minus cells, fluid = duct minus plate. Flow along +Z.
Faces classified by exact plane test, not by bounding-box side. Let me group them and check areas against hand values.
Scaling to metres once, then exporting the STEP and one STL per patch.
Now the coarse mesh in gmsh: 3 mm in the core, 6 mm in the ducts, physical surfaces from the same classification.
All 554 surfaces landed in one group — the classification test failed, so let me check what coordinates gmsh actually sees.
gmsh pads each bounding box by its 1e-7 tolerance. Widening the test to 1e-6 m and silencing the log.
Groups match the build123d face counts exactly. Now convert to OpenFOAM and check the coarse mesh.
Coarse mesh is topologically clean and the volume matches the CAD exactly. Let me look at it before refining.
Shape is right. Now the refined mesh: 1.5 mm in the core (≈5 cells across a channel), 3 mm in the ducts.
Setting the two wall patches to type `wall`, and measuring the stated dimensions back off the built solid.
The four STLs were tessellated per group, so shared edges may not match. I'll rewrite them from the single conformal gmsh surface mesh instead.
Let me verify the welded union myself: free edges and winding consistency across all four STLs.
Closed and consistently wound. Checking which way the union faces, via signed volume.

Mesh is built and verified. Summary:

**Built** (all in metres; CAD authored in mm and scaled ×0.001 once at export): square duct 80 × 80 mm running from z = −40 mm (inlet) through the 20 mm honeycomb core at z ∈ [0, 20] to z = +100 mm (outlet) — 40 mm upstream, 80 mm downstream as asked. Fluid = duct box − honeycomb plate; the plate is the 80×80×20 core box minus 93 hexagonal prisms cut through the full 20 mm.

**Measured from my own geometry, against the request:** interior cell 8.0000 mm across flats (asked 8); cell pitch 9.0 mm ⇒ wall thickness 1.0000 mm (asked 1); duct section 80.0 × 80.0 mm; core 20 mm thick with plate volume 34741.8 mm³ exactly equal to (core box − open area × 20 mm), i.e. every cell is open front to back. Fluid volume 8.612582e-4 m³ matches the CAD solid to 1e-10. Open area ratio 72.9 %. Patch areas: inlet 0.0064 m², outlet 0.0064 m², ductwalls 0.0384 m² (= 4×80×120 mm², no duct wall inside the core since the plate meets it), honeycomb 0.052933 m² (cell sides 49459.3 + two end faces 3474.2 mm²) — each named where the face was classified by an exact plane test, and the gmsh group counts (1/1/8/544) equal the build123d face counts.

**Mesh:** gmsh tet mesh, 425 767 cells, 1.5 mm in the core (≈5 cells across an 8 mm channel), 3 mm in the ducts; `gmshToFoam`; checkMesh "Mesh OK" (max non-orthogonality 69.0, max skewness 1.13). Patches `inlet`, `outlet` type patch; `ductwalls`, `honeycomb` type wall. The four STLs are cut from the single conformal surface mesh; I verified the union has 0 free edges, 0 same-direction duplicate edges, and outward normals.

**Assumptions I chose, not given:** flow along +z with inlet at the upstream end; the honeycomb lattice is centred on the duct axis with cells clipped to the section inset by one wall thickness (1 mm minimum wall to the duct), and clipped fragments smaller than 40 % of a full cell discarded into solid — smallest retained fragment is 50 %, which is why there are no slivers; mesh sizes; STL/tessellation tolerances. **Not checked:** no boundary-layer resolution was added (pure tet mesh), and I did not verify suitability for any particular solver or y+.
